Analyze rater-by-criterion halo-effect networks

Source: R/api-reports.R
rater_halo_network_analysis.Rd

Analyze rater-by-criterion halo-effect networks

Usage

rater_halo_network_analysis(
  fit,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  rater_facet = NULL,
  criterion_facet = NULL,
  context_facets = NULL,
  method = c("spearman", "pearson", "kendall"),
  min_pair_n = 5,
  alpha = 0.05,
  p_adjust = "bonferroni",
  min_abs_weight = 0,
  halo_weight_review = 0.5,
  halo_contrast_review = 0.1,
  min_retained_halo_edges = 1,
  positive_only = TRUE,
  include_graph = FALSE,
  bootstrap = 0L,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  seed = NULL,
  halo_reference = c("different_criteria", "all")
)

Arguments

fit

Output from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional output from diagnose_mfrm().

rater_facet

Name of the rater-like facet.

criterion_facet

Name of the criterion, rubric, task, or item-like facet used to form rater-by-criterion nodes.

context_facets

Facets defining rows in the reshaped wide matrix. Defaults to the person facet plus any facets other than the rater and criterion facets. Include "Person" for the independent-Person association screen; without it, correlations remain descriptive.

method

Correlation method used for rater-by-criterion node pairs.

min_pair_n

Minimum shared contexts required to estimate a node-pair relationship.

alpha

Adjusted p-value threshold for retaining edges. Set to 1 to disable p-value filtering, including when inference is unavailable; shared-count, weight and sign filters still apply. This changes retained-edge counts, graph topology, and graph centrality, but not the full-pair halo/non-halo distribution summaries.

p_adjust

Multiple-comparison adjustment passed to stats::p.adjust(). The default "bonferroni" follows the conservative screening used in Lamprianou's halo-network example.

min_abs_weight

Minimum absolute correlation retained as a graph edge. Like alpha, this is an analysis filter for the retained graph, not merely a display filter.

halo_weight_review

Same-rater cross-criterion mean absolute correlation at or above which a rater is marked for review. This is a package screening default, not a validated halo cut point.

halo_contrast_review

Minimum difference between a rater's mean halo edge weight and incident non-halo edge weight for a stronger review flag. This is a package screening default, not a validated halo cut point.

min_retained_halo_edges

Minimum retained halo edges required before a strong "warning" status is assigned.

positive_only

If TRUE, negative correlations are kept in pair_metrics but excluded from the graph edge table and retained-edge counts. Unfiltered distribution and per-rater summaries use absolute correlations regardless of this setting; inspect MeanSignedHaloWeight before interpreting a review flag.

include_graph

If TRUE, include the underlying igraph object.

bootstrap

Number of person-cluster resamples for the halo contrast; 0 (default) requests no interval. At least 199 when requested; use 999 or more for reporting and assess Monte Carlo stability.

conf_level

Confidence level for the pointwise percentile interval.

seed

Optional seed, preserving the caller's RNG state.

halo_reference

"different_criteria" compares within-rater cross-criterion correlations with between-rater cross-criterion correlations. "all" also includes same-criterion between-rater edges, matching the paper's descriptive all-non-halo reference.

Value

A bundle of class mfrm_halo_network containing:

summary

One-row halo-network summary and halo/non-halo contrast.

node_metrics

Rater-by-criterion node strength and graph-theoretic centrality.

edge_metrics

Retained graph edges.

pair_metrics

All estimated node-pair correlations with explicit retention flags for each graph filter, shared-context and Person counts, and p-value availability reasons. RetainedByP is TRUE for every pair when the p filter is disabled by alpha = 1.

halo_summary_by_rater

Per-rater summaries of same-rater criterion-pair edges, including ReviewStatus and ReviewReason.

caveats

Interpretation notes.

Details

rater_halo_network_analysis() reshapes rating data so that each rater-by-criterion combination is a node. Edges are correlations between those node score vectors across shared contexts. Edges connecting two nodes from the same rater but different criteria are labelled "halo"; all other retained edges are labelled "non_halo".

This response-profile network does not evaluate assignment connectedness or establish a common scale. Its degree, strength, betweenness, and closeness columns are graph-theoretic centrality summaries after adjusted-p, min_abs_weight, and sign filters are applied.

Per-rater ReviewStatus combines same-rater cross-criterion mean weight, incident non-halo comparison weight, and the number of retained halo edges. A "warning" means these criteria converge strongly enough to prioritize follow-up; "review" means at least one screening criterion is elevated. Neither label is a causal halo diagnosis, and the default review thresholds are package conventions rather than validated decision rules. Strong negative same-rater correlations are anomalous but are not evidence of a positive halo pattern; consult signed correlations in pair_metrics and MeanSignedHaloWeight.

The key descriptive comparison is the distribution of halo-edge weights versus non-halo-edge weights. A larger halo-edge distribution is consistent with a halo pattern, but this function deliberately reports it as a screening diagnostic. MeanHaloWeight and MeanNonHaloWeight use all finite absolute correlations meeting min_pair_n, before adjusted-p, min_abs_weight, and sign filtering; the corresponding MeanRetained* columns describe the filtered graph. Candidate and unavailable pair counts accompany these available-pair means. An incomplete comparison cannot receive an unqualified no-flag assessment.

WelchT, WelchDF and WelchP remain as unavailable compatibility columns. The correlations share observations, raters and nodes; an independent-sample test of their difference is not supplied. Pairwise correlation tail areas screen association under their sampling assumptions, not halo itself. For each pair, these tail areas require "Person" in context_facets and no repeated Person among its shared contexts. Otherwise the correlation is retained but PValue and PAdjusted are unavailable. N counts shared contexts, Persons counts distinct Persons when traceable, and PValueStatus explains availability. Repeating a Person across tasks does not create independent observations. No clustered test is substituted. Distinct identifiers do not establish independence: sampling dependence, fixed rater effects, ties and small-sample approximations still require review. Adjustments use the family of available pairwise p-values; counts of available and unavailable p-values are separate from correlation counts.

With alpha < 1, an unavailable p-value excludes that pair from the graph and prevents an unqualified "ok" review for an affected rater. alpha = 1 explicitly requests a descriptive graph without the p filter; it does not make the missing p-values available or validate review flags. No retained graph edges is not evidence that halo is absent; retain the originally specified thresholds. Recreate older network results from the existing fit and matching diagnostics before summary, plotting or export.

The node vectors contain observed scores, not model residuals. Repeated ratings within a context-by-node cell are averaged using observation weights; the selected correlation then compares available context means. Ability differences, related criteria and the assignment design can produce strong associations without a causal halo effect. Graph centrality here is distinct from middle-category use measured by rater_centrality_table().

A horn effect refers to an unfavorable impression spreading to ratings on other criteria. It is not a negative criterion correlation or simply high rater severity: lowering several criteria together can still produce positive correlations. Neither the sign of a network edge nor Infit/Outfit classifies halo versus horn; this function provides no such classification.

Direct halo models are a separate approach. Jin and Chiu (2022) introduce the MRFM-H mixture Rasch facets model; Jin and Eckes (2025) distinguish general-impression and inadequate-criterion-discrimination mechanisms in MRFM-H(GI) and MRFM-H(ID). These models are not implemented here. Network summaries do not estimate their latent classes or adjust measurements for those mechanisms. See mfrmr_methods_reference for choosing the target.

Save the complete result with base::saveRDS() before repeated plotting. plot(out, type = "edge_distribution") shows available absolute correlations before edge filters; type = "halo_summary" uses the selected metric. type = "matrix" shows signed retained correlations on a -1 to 1 scale, with grey unavailable/filtered entries. These views support as_ggplot(); the network view uses base graphics or custom graphics from plot_data(). Plot payloads retain settings, caveats and denominators outside the figure. Export the result's data frames with utils::write.csv(); this standalone bundle is not an automatically included section of mfrm_report().

Dependence-aware halo contrasts

halo_contrast is the unweighted mean of signed same-rater correlations minus the mean of the declared between-rater reference correlations. It uses the original available pair set before p-value/sign/edge filtering; it may therefore differ from the legacy retained-edge summary. Report the actual criterion/overlap mix in contrast_pairs; the default removes same-criterion reference edges but does not balance unequal criterion-pair counts.

Bootstrap resampling draws whole persons, keeping all their contexts, raters and criteria together, and recomputes every fixed pair. Repeated draws of a person remain repeated observations. This preserves within-person dependence and shared-edge sampling dependence. It assumes independent, representative person clusters and conditions on the observed raters, criteria and pair set. It does not generalize to a population of raters, account for clustering of persons within schools, establish causal halo, or validate missingness assumptions. A person context must be retained for resampling.

bootstrap_draws retains every attempted replicate and its status. If any required correlation becomes undefined (e.g. constant bootstrap scores), the interval is withheld rather than conditioning on successful replicates or silently changing the target edge set. Few persons/sparse overlap can make this method unsuitable. Percentile intervals are approximate, pointwise and not selection-adjusted. No independent-edge Welch p-value is supplied.

Relation to MFRM and published network analyses

These are observed-score relationships, not fitted residuals or adjusted Rasch parameters. Lamprianou (2025) compares agreement, directional and rater-by-criterion networks with MFRM; a close empirical correspondence is not numerical equivalence. Signed alpha edges and weighted directional SWS/PUS indices are available here; fit_rater_network() supplies binary ERGM estimation. Halo-edge associations can reflect trait covariance and rubric overlap; rater_halo_network_analysis() offers person-cluster bootstrap contrasts instead of an independent-edge test. Use mfrm_residual_network() for residual associations and subset_connectivity_report() for prefit assignment links. See vignette("mfrmr-networks-and-reporting") for complementary views, paired overlap, direction and interpretation. plot.mfrm_bundle() documents custom layouts and display-only filters, which do not change the computed network.

References

Lai, E. R., Wolfe, E. W., & Vickers, D. (2015). Differentiation of illusory and true halo in writing scores. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 75(1), 102-125.

Lamprianou, I. (2025). Network Analysis for the investigation of rater effects in language assessment: A comparison of ChatGPT vs human raters. Research Methods in Applied Linguistics, 4, 100205.

Jin, K.-Y., & Chiu, M. M. (2022). A mixture Rasch facets model for rater's illusory halo effects. Behavior Research Methods, 54, 2750-2764. doi:10.3758/s13428-021-01721-3 . Direct model, not implemented here.

Jin, K.-Y., & Eckes, T. (2025). When raters generalize: Examining sources of halo effects with mixture Rasch facets models. Behavior Research Methods, 57, Article 149. doi:10.3758/s13428-025-02667-6 . Direct models, not implemented here.

See also

rater_network_analysis(), interrater_agreement_table(), plot.mfrm_bundle()

Examples

# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_core.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {
  halo <- rater_halo_network_analysis(fit)
  halo$summary
  head(halo$halo_summary_by_rater)
  plot(halo, type = "edge_distribution", draw = FALSE)
}
